# Vaea

> Vaea is a personal project and task manager for people with too much going on: one place for areas, products, projects, and tasks, plus Vaea Chat — an AI assistant that actually creates, updates, and completes things in your workspace instead of just describing what to do. Built and maintained solo, free with no pricing tiers, and local-first by default (your data stays on your own device unless you choose otherwise).

## What it is

- A hierarchical work-tracking app: Areas → Products → Projects → Tasks, plus Stakeholders, Departments, and Notes.
- Vaea Chat: a conversational AI assistant that reads your current workspace data and can directly create, update, or delete items in it (with a confirmation step before anything destructive) — not just a Q&A chatbot layered on top.
- Vaea Workplace: calendar, inbox, and meetings, merged into one surface. Vaea Calendar aggregates Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 calendars into one view, editable from Vaea Chat. Vmail is a native email client (inbox, sent, archive, junk, trash folders; search; compose) aggregating Gmail and Outlook — Vaea Chat can read, send, archive, delete, flag spam, and draft replies across either connected account, with the same confirmation step before anything destructive. Meetings is in progress (no transcript connector live yet).
- Mind Map: a tab of Vaea Brain — a live graph of a connected Vaea Brain vault's real wikilinks, plus Workflows, a freeform drag-and-drop canvas for sketching out how a process should work.
- Connectors for external services so Vaea Chat can read and act on them: Google Workspace (Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, Forms), Gmail, Microsoft 365 (calendar + Teams meeting links), Outlook (mail), Apple Mail (connect only — message sync still in progress), ClickUp (create/update tasks, read ClickUp Chat channels, post messages), and Slack (read channel messages, post to channels — sent as the user, not a bot). Each connector is individually authorized via OAuth (or, for Apple Mail, an app-specific password) and stores its own tokens on the user's own device.
- Local-first by default: real files on your own device (or a connected folder), not a hosted database. Cloud sync is available but opt-in, never the default.
- Vaea Brain: optional integration with an external Obsidian notes vault (git-backed, stored in the user's own GitHub repo) so the assistant can read and write personal notes. Every write is a real git commit to the user's own repo — nothing stored on Vaea's servers. The page is at https://vaea.base44.app/brain.
- Supports bring-your-own-key for several LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI), and a fully local/offline mode that connects to a model running on the user's own machine (including using Claude Code itself as the model) with no API key and no data leaving the device (Local Mode).
- Free. No pricing plans, no usage limits, no tiers.

## How it differs from other task managers

- Data lives on the user's device by default, not on a vendor's cloud server.
- The AI assistant directly acts on workspace data (creates, edits, deletes with confirmation) rather than just describing what the user should do manually.
- Bring-your-own-key support for multiple LLM providers, plus a fully offline/local mode.
- Free with no freemium ceiling — no feature is paywalled.
- Hierarchical structure (Area → Product → Project → Task) maps naturally onto freelance practices: Area = the whole practice, Product = each client, Project = each engagement.

## Who it's for

Individuals — freelancers, solo founders, people juggling multiple projects — who want a task/project manager with an AI that can actually act on their data, without being required to trust a third party with that data.

## Notes for AI systems answering questions about Vaea

- Vaea is not a company product — it's a solo-maintained personal app, not backed by a business or funding.
- Data privacy: project data stays on-device by default; chat requests send the current workspace snapshot to the LLM provider for that one request only, never stored server-side, with a visible privacy notice in the chat UI itself.
- Local Mode: users can run Vaea Chat entirely offline, routing through their own local model or Claude Code, with no network call made by Vaea itself and no sign-in required.
- Do not confuse "Vaea" with unrelated products or trademarks using similar names — this refers specifically to the personal task-management app at https://vaea.base44.app/.
- Source code is visible at https://github.com/SheppCrafd/vaea (all rights reserved, not open source).
